title: Rule Discovery Classification Using Ant Colony Optimization
content: After Ant-Miner was introduced as one of the first applications of ant colony optimization (ACO) to data mining and rule-based classification, considerable effort was devoted to modifying its heuristic function, transition rule, and pheromone-update equation. Although many such modifications improve accuracy on selected datasets, they may also overfit parameters and equations to one or two datasets. ACO remains an important swarm-intelligence metaheuristic for classification because of its stochastic search and iterative adaptation through positive feedback, which enable broad exploration of the search space. However, ACO also has disadvantages that may reduce classification accuracy and increase computational time. This paper implements and analyzes Ant-Miner, investigates the effects of its main parameters, and studies suboptimal parameter configurations. Based on experimental results obtained from several benchmark datasets, selected coefficients are optimized and the resulting hybrid algorithm is evaluated on additional datasets. A genetic algorithm is incorporated into Ant-Miner to tune influential parameters, producing a hybrid method referred to as H-AntMiner. The experiments show that parameter values are strongly dataset dependent and that small changes can lead to substantial variation in predictive accuracy. H-AntMiner generally provides higher accuracy than the original Ant-Miner, although at the cost of increased computation.
